sessions.summary: DEFECT found and fixed, logged separately (not folded into Phase 8 feature list). Bug: routes.lead_id had no UNIQUE constraint (only plain non-unique ix_routes_lead_id); route_lead() inserted a new Route on every act() call, and act() called it even when create_or_update_lead returned lead_op="updated", so a second act() for the same lead (reachable via FR-2 edited-resubmission path) created a SECOND routes row; reachable since Phase 6; found by diagnostic review, not the test suite. Fix: Alembic 0009_routes_lead_id_unique adds UNIQUE constraint uq_routes_lead_id on routes.lead_id replacing the redundant non-unique index and dedupes legacy duplicates; Route.__table_args__ updated; route_lead() is now an upsert (update queue/rule_matched/sla_deadline on re-route, else insert). Correction per "correction-of-a-correction": route_lead() returns (route, "created"|"updated") tuple and act() writes routed on create and route_updated on an in-place update (added route_updated to VALID_ACTION_TYPES); no dashboard.py change needed since the allowlist ignores unlisted action_types.

sessions.phase_name: Phase 8 pre-work - events_created reconciliation mismatch defect fix
sessions.summary: SEPARATE DEFECT from S0013 (routes fix) with a distinct root cause, found during the same diagnostic session; logged as its own entry. Bug: the events_created dashboard count filtered on Event.is_valid.is_(True), Event.is_edit.is_(False), treating created/edited as mutually exclusive; but every valid event was created AND some were later ALSO edited (both immutable facts matching event_created / event_edited receipts). When an FR-2 edit flips is_edit to True the row dropped out of events_created, producing nonzero variance (events_created: dashboard_count=0, receipt_count=1). Not caught by the original suite: no test combined create + edit + reconciliation. Fix: events_created query now filters ONLY on is_valid.is_(True); events_edited unchanged (is_edit monotonic). events_created and events_edited are now intentionally OVERLAPPING (not a partition) - correct model, not a double-count bug.
sessions.verification: New regression test test_create_then_edit_keeps_reconciliation_variance_zero: POST valid event -> reconciliation ok/0; then edit same event -> STILL ok/0 with both events_created and events_edited at 0. Verified fails against pre-fix query (overall_status mismatch, events_created variance 1) and passes with fix. Reconciliation file 6 passed; full suite 92 passed, 1 skipped (91 prior + 1 new).

sessions.phase_name: Phase 8b - Retry/Backoff + Dead-Letter for the Interpret Stage (FR-11)
sessions.summary: DeadLetterQueue model (table dead_letter_queue: id PK, event_id FK, stage, error, retry_count, resolved default false, created_at); Alembic 0010_dead_letter_queue (down_revision 0009). interpret.py: on retry exhaustion (bounded by _is_retryable) the event is dead-lettered - a dead_letter_queue row (stage="interpret", sanitized/truncated error <=500 chars, retry_count=actual attempts) plus a dead_lettered receipt in a SINGLE commit (FR-9 atomicity), replacing the previous interpreted/status=error receipt. Per-attempt backoffs logged via structlog, not receipted. Retry config env-configurable: retry_max_attempts (default 3) and retry_base_delay_ms (default 500) from RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS/RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS. events.py + schemas/responses.py: exhaustion returns status="dead_letter", stage="interpret"; pipeline halts (confirmed short-circuit already prevented score/act). dashboard.py: added dead_letter_queue reconciliation pair (dead_letter_queue <-> dead_lettered). Finding: "error" is never used as an action_type anywhere (only as a status); retiring error-as-action_type was a no-op; exhaustion receipt uses action_type="dead_lettered", status="error". Decision: dead_letter_queue IS a reconciliation pair (row vs dead_lettered receipt, written atomically 1:1) added deliberately and disclosed.

sessions.summary: app/routers/admin.py (new; mounted in main.py after external routers, matching no-prefix-at-mount convention since each router bakes its own prefix). POST /api/v1/admin/replay/{event_id}: bearer-token gated, re-runs existing pipeline (classify_event -> score_event -> act) by REUSING the service functions; on success marks DLQ row resolved=true, writes a dead_letter_resolved receipt (entity_type="dead_letter"), returns 200 {status: replayed, event_id, lead_id}. POST /api/v1/admin/simulate-failure: body {stage, event_id}; for stage="interpret" writes a DLQ row + dead_lettered receipt and returns 200 {status: dead_lettered} (test-harness without a real provider call); rejects non-interpret stages with 400 invalid_stage. receipts.py: dead_letter_resolved added to VALID_ACTION_TYPES. sessions.summary: Audit of Phases 0-8 against PRD v1.2 and the implementation plan, then fixes for every issue found (6 defects reported + a 7th surfaced while fixing). D1 payload_hash not advanced on edit (ingest.py): the column is the stored comparand for future submissions on the same dedupe_key, so the row stayed permanently unequal to its own content - the edited payload re-detected as an edit forever (extra event_edited receipt + redundant interpret/score/act each time, unbounded reconciliation variance) while the original payload was misread as a duplicate, silently discarding a revert; fix advances the hash and records previous_payload_hash + payload_hash in the receipt metadata. D2 create_new review resolution minted an Identity with no identity_created receipt (FR-9 violation; identities vs identity_created pair permanently nonzero); fix writes the receipt with match_rule=manual_review_resolve, match_confidence=1.00, review_id, plus the structured log line, and derives display_name from the event's identity_fields. D3 resolving a manual review never resumed the pipeline (Flow 3 step 4): ingest halts an ambiguous event before interpret, so resolution is the only thing that can un-halt it, but resolve only linked the identity - the event was left with no interpretation/score/lead/route/touch permanently. Fix extracts app/services/pipeline.py::run_downstream as the single shared interpret->score->act runner and points all three entry points at it (ingest, manual-review resume, admin replay) so they cannot drift; ingest and resume surface exhausted retries as 202 status=dead_letter, replay keeps 503 replay_failed; resolve now returns pipeline_status/label/score/decision_outcome/lead_id/lead_op/queue/rule_matched/sla_deadline/attribution_touch_id per the PRD API table. D4 UNIQUE(events.dedupe_key) was global, not scoped to accepted rows - two symptoms from one cause: (a) resubmitting the same schema-invalid payload raised IntegrityError -> 500, breaking 'never silently drop an invalid event' since the caller got an error instead of a persisted rejection; (b) a corrected resubmission matched the rejected row's dedupe_key and was treated as an EDIT of a row still flagged is_valid=false, running the pipeline against it and never producing a clean accepted event. Fix: migration 0011 replaces the constraint with a partial unique index WHERE is_valid = true AND dedupe_key IS NOT NULL, and find_event_by_dedupe_key is scoped to is_valid = true to match. Considered and rejected: catching IntegrityError in persist_invalid_event and collapsing repeat rejections onto one row - fixes only (a), leaves (b), and desynchronizes the events_rejected vs event_rejected pair (one row, N receipts). The migration looks the auto-generated constraint name up from pg_constraint rather than hardcoding events_dedupe_key_key; downgrade() NULLs duplicate dedupe_keys (keeping the oldest valid row) before restoring the global constraint so no audit row is deleted. D5 routes.escalated was never evaluated - three docstrings described it as computed-on-read but nothing computed it, escalated was absent from the /leads list payload, and FR-9's escalated action type was missing from VALID_ACTION_TYPES so the transition could not have been receipted. Fix: new app/services/escalation.py with a pure is_sla_breached (strict <, so exactly on the deadline is not yet breached, matching the >=-at-threshold convention in resolve.should_auto_link and score._decide; naive timestamps coerced to UTC rather than raising) and evaluate_escalation performing a monotonic false->true transition, writing the escalated receipt once, not committing (caller owns the transaction). On-read detection rather than a scheduler is the PRD's own recommendation (section 12 open item, line 421) - no new dependency. D6 manual_review_queue.resolved_at left NULL on resolution; fixed in the same resolve_review rewrite, both branches now commit exactly once. D7 (found while fixing) events_edited reconciliation manufactured variance: events.is_edit is a sticky boolean so the entity side counts 'ever edited' while the receipt side counted raw event_edited receipts - any twice-edited event reported variance 1 and failed the FR-10 / success-criterion-2 gate. Fixed with COUNT(DISTINCT receipts.event_id) on that pair only; all 8 pairs audited, it is the only one affected. API gaps closed: GET /api/v1/dead-letter (new app/routers/dead_letter.py) - the PRD Error States table promises a dead-lettered event is visible there, but Phase 8b wrote the rows and 8c added replay with nothing able to enumerate what needed replaying without direct SQL; read-only and unauthenticated (PRD lists 200 only; the bearer gate covers the mutating admin endpoints), ?resolved= filtered, oldest-first because the list doubles as a replay worklist, each entry carrying a replay_url. /dashboard/reconciliation now returns the PRD's top-level {variance, status: PASS|FAIL} alongside the FR-10 per-metric rows and accepts since/until applied to BOTH sides of every comparison - exact because Postgres evaluates now() once per transaction and an entity plus its receipt are written in one transaction, so a window cannot split a pair; overall_status and total_variance retained as aliases. Deliberately NOT added: interpreted/scored reconciliation pairs, since those receipts accumulate per re-run while the row count stays at 1 (interpretations.event_id is UNIQUE), which would break the variance-0 gate by construction. Compliance (Phase 1 / Phase 3 gates): README.md now carries the LIVE/SIMULATED/TEST/MOCKED table at the point of use - all three connectors SIMULATED (internal fixture generators, no Reddit/social/ESP API ever called), classification LIVE via OpenRouter, simulate-failure test-harness-only, test-suite LLM calls MOCKED - plus the two efficiency short-circuits that mean not every event triggers the LIVE call, and a migration note for 0011. Out of scope on purpose: /api/v1/dashboard/summary and the Jinja2 dashboard screens are Phase 9 per the implementation plan.
